title: Implement credential-gated end-to-end Alpaca paper integration suite
description:
Write a credential-gated Alpaca PAPER integration suite that drives the real production broker adapter against the Alpaca paper environment, plus an offline end-to-end test of the protective-order and live-mode guards. Without paper credentials and explicit operator approval, the paper suite must skip cleanly with a visible reason. It must never contact the live endpoint.

Before editing, inspect:
- mike_trade/brokers/ (Alpaca trading adapter, paper/live endpoint selection, trade_updates stream handling, capability declarations)
- mike_trade/protection/ or equivalent (fixed stop, native trailing stop, stepped trailing stop coordinators)
- mike_trade/execution/ and mike_trade/reconciliation/ (order intents, fill ingestion, idempotent activity matching, drift detection)
- mike_trade/app.py and mike_trade/runtime.py (as wired by t.3)
- mike_trade/controls/service_manager.py (live confirmation handling from t.1)
- docs/ALPACA.md (capability matrix and setup from t.4)
- tests/conftest.py and existing tests/end_to_end/ fixtures

Implementation requirements:
1. tests/paper_broker/test_alpaca_paper_cycle.py:
   - Gate on all of: paper key/secret env vars present; an explicit opt-in approval env var (for example MIKE_TRADE_PAPER_ORDERS_APPROVED=1); and a resolved trading base URL that is the Alpaca paper endpoint. Otherwise call pytest.skip with a message stating which precondition is missing. Never mark these as passed when skipped.
   - Assert hard that the configured mode is PAPER and that the endpoint is not the live API host. Abort the module if any LIVE credential variable is set, so live credentials cannot be used by mistake.
   - Use one operator-specified liquid symbol and a bounded small notional/quantity. Check market hours/clock and skip if the market is closed.
   - Run the real lifecycle through production components: entry intent -> paper buy submission -> trade_updates/order polling reconciliation of fills (including partial fill handling when observed) -> protective order placement covering the actual filled quantity -> discretionary sell that coordinates cancellation/replacement of protection without overselling -> verify the position is flat and the ledger matches broker activities exactly once.
   - Parameterize the protective combinations that the provider capability matrix declares supported: fixed stop, broker-native trailing stop, and provider-neutral stepped trailing (verify each step only moves upward). For combinations declared unsupported or unverified (for example fractional quantity with a stop or trailing order), assert that the application fails closed and reports them as blocked rather than submitting.
   - Verify Decimal precision handling for whole and fractional quantities and price increments against the broker responses.
   - Clean up in a finally/fixture teardown: cancel only orders created by the test and close only the test position, using the paper account.
2. tests/end_to_end/test_protective_live_guards.py (offline, no network, no credentials):
   - Use the production runtime with the shadow/simulated broker or an injected adapter that records calls (not a mock-only claim of Alpaca integration) to prove: a protective order is created only after a confirmed positive fill and covers the actual remaining quantity on partial fills; a long stop never moves downward; overlapping discretionary/manual exit and stop cannot produce a net short position; unknown stop state blocks new entries; unsupported fractional/order combinations fail closed; LIVE mode refuses to start or mutate without explicit live authorization; PAPER and LIVE credentials, endpoints, and ledgers never cross; and shutdown leaves valid protective stops untouched.
   - Include negative cases for each guard.
3. Make sure no test in this task can run in CI without credentials and approval and still hit the network.
acceptance_criteria: tests/paper_broker/test_alpaca_paper_cycle.py skips with an explicit reason when paper credentials or the explicit order-approval opt-in are absent, and never reports pass in that state.
The paper suite asserts that the resolved trading endpoint is the Alpaca paper host and aborts if any live credential variable is present or the endpoint is the live host.

With credentials and approval present, the paper suite exercises buy -> fill reconciliation -> protective order on actual filled quantity -> coordinated sell -> flat position -> ledger matched to broker activities exactly once, using production adapter/coordinator classes rather than mocks.

The paper suite parameterizes fixed, native trailing, and stepped trailing protection according to declared provider capabilities, and asserts that unsupported or unverified combinations are blocked rather than submitted.
The paper suite teardown cancels and closes only test-created paper orders and positions.

tests/end_to_end/test_protective_live_guards.py runs fully offline without credentials and contains positive and negative tests for: post-fill protection on partial fills, monotonic non-decreasing long stop, no oversell on overlapping exits, unknown-stop entry block, fractional fail-closed, live-authorization refusal, paper/live isolation, and shutdown leaving protective stops untouched.
Neither test file contains hardcoded credentials or a live Alpaca endpoint used for order submission.
forbidden_changes: change PLAN_SKELETON.json or any planning artifacts under .abracapocus/
submit orders to the Alpaca live endpoint or read live credentials
run the paper suite without operator-supplied paper credentials and explicit approval
replace the production Alpaca adapter with mocks and present that as broker integration
claim fake provider capabilities to make tests pass
run broad test suites or backtests as incidental verification
